headline: Genome assemblies and metabolic models reveal fungal and bacterial adaptation traits
label: Fungal Genomics And Metabolism
summary: Chromosome-level and pangenome-based resources now link genome structure to nutrient use and secondary metabolite traits in plant-associated microbes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of resolved genome structure, from pangenome-derived models to chromosome-level assemblies, to explain how microbes and fungi adapt their metabolism to their environment. The Xylella fastidiosa iXfcore model, built from a pangenome core and validated in defined media, identifies acetate-supported growth and polyamine secretion. The Fusarium oxysporum FO12 assembly, generated from Nanopore and Hi-C data, provides a 57.60 Mb genome in 14 scaffolds with resolved centromeres for a biocontrol strain. The Verticillium dahliae study links an NRPS-like secondary metabolite gene cluster to adaptation across different nutrient environments. The Mus81 study addresses RNA editing and DNA repair tradeoffs in heat tolerance and meiosis, a more indirect connection to genome resolution. What is new is the coupling of genome-scale structure to specific metabolic and stress-adaptation phenotypes rather than a shared methodological advance.
